# Goal entry

What a goal needs, what can’t be saved and who may save it: one rule for New goal, the edit page, set-up’s cards, a spreadsheet’s Goals rows and the AI tools, in the same words.

## The rule

Every way a goal comes in asks the same rule, in the same words: New goal, the edit page, set-up's goal cards, a Goals row of a spreadsheet, Data or a bulk edit (the change engine, `planChanges`), and the AI tools (which use the change engine). The form saves through `planGoal`, run by the `saveGoal` action, so it can't save what the engine would refuse.

**Who may (rule 7).** Anyone may add a goal for anyone, at any level, at every door (Lane, 11 Nov: `mayAddGoal` is always yes, and is the one place that is said). Changing a goal stays with its owner and admins (`mayChangeGoal`), whoever made it; New goal says so as soon as someone else is chosen as owner: “Amara will own it. After it is published, only Amara or an admin can change it.”

**What a field needs (rule 1).** Read from the spreadsheet's field table (`fieldNeed`): required, optional, worked out, or not asked for this type. In the form, a field that always shows a value (the type, the team, the level, which side a range keeps to) is required. Optional fields say “· optional” after their label; a step with two or more required fields and at least one optional says “Everything here is needed unless it says optional.” under its heading. The unit is optional and starts empty: a number has no unit by default, never “%”.

**What can't be saved (rule 2, `goalMustFix`).** Each problem is under its own field, in the form's order. The name (at least three characters), an owner, a team (“{Owner} isn’t in a team. Choose the team this goal is for.” when the owner has none), a level, a link that would make a loop; for a number to move, where it starts (“Enter where it starts today.”; on the edit page “Enter where it starts.”) and a target that differs from it (“The target is the same as today (40%). To hold a number where it is, make this a number to keep in range.”, offering to); for a range, the limit, and a warning margin of zero or more (empty is none); for stages, at least one, each with a name, a name no other stage has (compared without case or accents), and a due week in the year. A stage done in a check-in can't be removed, and fewer decimal places than check-ins already have is refused.

**A number as typed (rule 12, `numberAsTyped`).** Digits as people type them (a decimal comma, thousands, a sign); words after it only when they are the goal's unit (“12 days” in a days goal, with min and mins, day and days, hr and hours the same; “12%” in a % goal). Anything else after the digits is “has words”: “12 days” has words in it. Type the number only, like 12; this goal counts %. Letters in place of digits are “not a number”, with an example at the goal's decimal places.

**Decimals, worked out (`decimalsFor`).** The places chosen; or, when none were, the most typed in Today, Target or Limit, at most 3, said in one line (“Kept to 1 decimal place, as you typed them.”) with Change. A number with more places than chosen is refused, offering to keep them.

**Whether a step goes on (rule 4, `stepState`).** The button is never disabled. Pressed with a Must fix on its step, every field of the step shows its own, focus goes to the first, and one line above the button counts them: “2 things to fix above: Unit and Target.” (more than three: the first two “and {k} more”), the same line the check-in uses. A Must fix shows under a field once it has been changed and left, never while typing.

**Saving (rule 7, `planGoal`).** Refused, in these words, unless the actor may, nothing must be fixed, the plan's question (domain/goal `planQuestion`) has its yes, and a plan change after check-ins have started has a reason (“Say why, in a sentence. It goes in the goal’s History, and anyone watching it sees the change flagged.”). Then one commit: the goal (a new one with the workspace's next key), its History entry with Why, and a new goal's stages already done.

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Unit and Start for a number to move; Unit for dated stages; Margin for a range (the field table’s needs). | `required as start, optional as unit; not-asked; optional` |
| Whether step 3 of a number goal with no metric, and step 1, say “Everything here is needed unless it says optional.” | `yes; no` |
| “12”, “1,250.5”, “29,4”, “12%” in a % goal; “12 days” in a days goal, “12 mins” in a min goal; “12 days” in a % goal and with no unit; “12%” in a days goal; “abc”, “1.2.3”, “12-”. | `12, 1250.5, 29.4, 12; 12, 12; has-words, has-words; has-words; not-number, not-number, not-number` |
| A name of “ab”. | `name-short: Give the goal a name of at least three characters.` |
| A number goal, unit %, today “12 days”, target 30. | `has-words: “12 days” has words in it. Type the number only, like 12; this goal counts %.` |
| Unit “days”, today “12 days”, target 5. | `nothing` |
| Unit %, today “1,5”, target 3, decimals not chosen; then decimals chosen as whole numbers. | `nothing / too-precise: 1,5 has 1 decimal place, but this goal keeps whole numbers, so it would show as 2. Type 2, or keep 1 decimal place for this goal.` |
| Today “abc”, target 30, whole numbers. | `not-number: “abc” isn’t a number. Type digits only, like 29.` |
| Today 40, target 40, unit %. | `same-as-start: The target is the same as today (40%). To hold a number where it is, make this a number to keep in range.` |
| Stages “Design” in week 48 and “design ” in week 50; then “Design” with no week. | `stage-twice: Two stages are called “Design”. Give each its own name, such as “design review”. / stage-week: Choose the week “Design” is due.` |
| A file’s stage “Design” due in week 60 of a 53-week year. | `stage-week: “Design” needs a due week between 1 and 53: it says “60”.` |
| An owner in no team, the team empty. | `team-empty: Amara Nwosu isn’t in a team. Choose the team this goal is for.` |
| A range with a warning margin of −1. | `margin-negative: Enter a warning margin of zero or more, or leave it empty.` |
| Step 3 with Unit empty but no Today, and Target “30 mins” in a % goal; four Must fix on one step. | `2 things to fix above: Today and Target. / 4 things to fix above: Today, Target and 2 more.` |
| Tunde (not an admin) saves a new north star owned by Amara through the saveGoal action; then a spreadsheet row of the same; then Tunde changes a goal Amara owns. | `saved, G-127 owned by amara / no problems / refused: Only Rhea Kapoor (its owner) or an admin can change` |

## Requirements

- `GOAL-ENTRY-REQUIRED`: Every way of adding a goal says what it needs before it is refused, checks it with one rule, and asks rather than assumes where a value is possible but unlikely; nothing is saved before it has been read back.

- what a field needs (rule 1) › reads the field table: Unit optional for a number, not asked for stages; Margin optional for a range

- a number as typed (rule 12) › reads “%s” in a goal counting “%s”
- a number as typed (rule 12) › says “%s” has words in a goal counting “%s”

- what can’t be saved (rule 2) › gives each of the worked examples

- what can’t be saved (rule 2) › says each stage row’s own fault under it
- what can’t be saved (rule 2) › refuses fewer decimal places than check-ins already have
- what can’t be saved (rule 2) › treats an empty margin as none, and a negative one as a Must fix
- whether a step goes on (rule 4) › counts each field with a Must fix, in the form’s order, and names the first to focus
- saving (rule 7) › saves a north star Tunde adds for Amara, with the next key and its History entry
- saving (rule 7) › refuses what must be fixed, in its words
- saving (rule 7) › lets only the owner or an admin change a goal
- saving (rule 7) › asks for a reason when the plan changes after check-ins have started, and keeps it as Why
- saving (rule 7) › gives back no commit when nothing changed
